match_note: Reviewer #1 quotes the title 'Versatile multi-q antiferromagnetic charge order in correlated vdW metals', which is the arXiv v1 title. The figure details referees cite all appear in v1: blue arrows in Fig. 2e, the ±22 meV line cuts in Fig. 2h, the +15 meV peak in Fig. 2g, the missing set current in Fig. 3e, mismatched set-points in Fig. 1f, and spectra normalized by the 0 to -30 mV area. R2 writes 'Fig. 3g' but means v1 Fig. 2g; the authors' strikeout correction confirms this. Rounds are Version 0 (R1, R2, R4 substantive; R3 is an early-career co-reviewer with no content), Version 2 (R1 minor points; R2 and R4 accept) and Version 3 (R1 accepts). The moiré title R1 objects to in round 2 was introduced in the revision and is not in v1.

concerns.quote: the author claims the observed CDW2mag and CBCmag are due to magnetic orders, however, there is no direct evidence to support it... It is better to use spin-polarized STM technique
concerns.summary: The magnetic structure below TN and above the spin-flop field is not characterized, so the claimed magnetic origin and intertwining mechanism lack direct evidence; spin-polarized STM is suggested.

concerns.quote: Several recent publications showcase the intertwining of magnetic and electronic orders in RTe3 materials... could the authors show more directly how the present work yields novel insights
concerns.summary: Spin-charge intertwining in RTe3 and CeTe3 has already been reported (Chillal TbTe3 X-ray/neutron; Higashihara CeTe3 transport), so the novelty beyond DOS maps is unclear.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the presented data appears to have come from a single set of measurements... did the Fourier intensities match when the field was ramped back down to 0 T
concerns.summary: The results seem to come from one measurement sequence; repeatability, including after ramping the field back to zero, is not shown, and RTe3 Fourier intensities are known to be tip-sensitive.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: All the dI/dV spectra shown are between -30 mV and +30 mV or so. Can the authors show 1-2 larger energy range spectra
concerns.summary: Wider-energy spectra are requested to show where the DOS above and below TN converges.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Missing setpoint information in Fig.3e
concerns.summary: The Fig. 3e caption lacks complete set-point information.

concerns.quote: can author present multiple energy slices of the dI/dV map so that one can check at which energy the checkerboard pattern of CBC1,2 is most prominent?
concerns.summary: dI/dV maps at multiple energies in the spin-flop phase are requested to find where the checkerboard is strongest.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: can the author shows dI/dV map at a fixed energy... with the magnetic field below and above spin-flop transition, so that one can visually see the competition of CDW2_mag and CBC in real space
concerns.summary: Fixed-energy dI/dV maps below and above the spin-flop field are requested to show the competition directly in real space.

concerns.quote: all dI/dV spectra are normalized by the area between 0 mV and -30 mV. It would be useful to also see a comparison with spectra which are not normalized
concerns.summary: Unnormalized spectra are requested to check that the area normalization does not drive the conclusions.

concerns.quote: Figure 1b shows for CeTe3, no CDW2 phase exists... Does it mean the refence 26 is wrong, or just because not going lower temperature? Is CDW2mag is same as CDW2?
concerns.summary: The phase diagram from the literature shows no CDW2 in CeTe3, which conflicts with the observed CDW2mag, and its relation to conventional CDW2 is unclear.

concerns.quote: The onset below TN cannot justify the CDW2mag due to magnetism, it can be other mechanism, for example the evolution of phonon spectrum.
concerns.summary: An onset coinciding with TN does not prove a magnetic origin; a non-magnetic mechanism such as phonon evolution could explain it.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Please note what the blue arrows in Fig. 2e stand for. And what is the abbreviation of "r.l.u."?... the label of horizontal axis in 2f is missing.
concerns.summary: Fig. 2 has undefined blue arrows, an undefined abbreviation and a missing axis label.

concerns.quote: please mark the pathway of line-cut profile of the measurement of Fig. 2f in Fig. 2d
concerns.summary: The momentum path (which l) of the Fig. 2f line cut is not indicated.

concerns.quote: If assuming the (0.0) position is for the central spot, what are the rest of three spots in panel d?
concerns.summary: Additional Fourier peaks near the center of the FT in Fig. 2d are not assigned.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: it doesn't consistence with Fig. 2f, I don't see the intensity peak at +15 meV in f panel. please explain.
concerns.summary: The +15 meV peak in the CDW2mag intensity plot does not appear in the energy-resolved line cut it is supposedly derived from.

concerns.quote: Is there any particular reason to compare the line-cut profile of the Fourier signal at ±22 meV in Fig. 2h?
concerns.summary: The choice of ±22 meV for the Fig. 2h comparison is unexplained.

concerns.quote: why not taken from dI/dV mapping of d panel, which at least could remove topographic contribution... The lattice of surface Te contribute to the image mostly
concerns.summary: Field-dependent Fourier analysis uses topographs dominated by the Te lattice rather than dI/dV maps, which would better isolate electronic contrast.

concerns.quote: A critical concern is, all topographic images of Fig. 1g, Fig. 3a, the Fig. 2a and 2c, the measuring setpoints are different... may cause some tip effect
concerns.summary: Topographs are compared across different set-points and therefore different tip-sample distances, which could create artifacts.

concerns.quote: How is the spatial evolution of dI/dV spectra?... please clarify how the measurement are performed and how spatially average being done.
concerns.summary: The spatial variation of spectra and the spatial averaging procedure are not described.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Bflop (~1.5 T) and TN (~1.5 K) is a relatively small energy, I doubt it can drive a FS deformation... The author need provide a confirmative speculation with solid evidence.
concerns.summary: Such small magnetic energy scales are unlikely to drive ±30 meV Fermi-surface and DOS reconstructions, and the listed mechanisms are speculative.

concerns.quote: the absence of quasiparticle interference measurements or electronic band calculations is a significant omission. Without these, it is difficult to convincingly disentangle the interplay
concerns.summary: Without QPI or band calculations, the proposed nesting picture linking charge and magnetic orders is not convincing.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the manuscript lacks a strong connection to the more exotic or topological multi-q phases referenced in the abstract and introduction... more appropriate for a specialized journal
concerns.summary: The claimed link to exotic or topological multi-q phases is not demonstrated, which weakens the case for a high-impact journal.

concerns.quote: Prior studies by the authors... report two AF transitions at approximately 3 K and 1 K. Does the sample in this study not exhibit a transition at 3 K?
concerns.summary: The previously reported second transition near 3 K is neither measured nor discussed, raising completeness and transparency concerns.

concerns.quote: they normalize I_CDW by I_Bragg, but the rationale for this is unclear. Wouldn't it be more appropriate to analyze the normalized conductance L=(dI/dV)/(I/V)
concerns.summary: The rationale for normalizing Fourier intensities by the Bragg peak is unclear; normalized conductance maps are suggested to mitigate set-point effects.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The discrepancy in the spin-flop field between magnetization and STM measurements suggests that the field may not lie strictly along the crystallographic axes
concerns.summary: The field orientation relative to the crystal axes is unspecified, and possible misalignment, hinted by the spin-flop field mismatch with magnetometry, must be ruled out.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The set-point parameters for the 4 K and 0.3 K data in Fig. 1f appear inconsistent. These should be aligned ideally.
concerns.summary: Spectra above and below TN were taken at different set-points, which compromises their comparison.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: The response file notes that raw dI/dV data... are shown in Fig. S7b. However, there is no Figure S7b... Are all the spectra shown in the manuscript now raw
later_concerns.summary: The rebuttal cites a nonexistent figure for the raw spectra, so it is unclear whether normalization is still applied.

later_concerns.quote: I cannot find a description of what constitutes moiré phases in this material... the "moiré" part should be removed from the title and the main text.
later_concerns.summary: The new 'electronic moiré phases' title is not justified by the content.

first_round.quote: In principle I am in favor of recommending this paper for publication if authors successfully address my concerns... For a journal of Nat. Commun.'s caliber showing repeatability would make the arguments a lot more convincing.

some important issues need to be addressed before considering the publication... I think the experimental results is not enough to support their claim... the author need provide more solid experimental evidence
I co-reviewed this manuscript with one of the reviewers who provided the listed reports.

the absence of quasiparticle interference measurements or electronic band calculations is a significant omission... I believe the work may be more appropriate for a specialized journal rather than Nature Communications.

recommendations.note: First round is Version 0. No transfer from another journal is indicated. The file then jumps to Version 2 and Version 3, with no Version 1 present. R1 says they favor publication, but they list 'Major comments' that ask for new repeatability data, wider-energy spectra and extra map slices. That requires substantial new data, so it is coded major revision. R2 says the claims are not yet supported, which could suggest reject. However, they frame it as issues to address 'before considering the publication' and ask for more evidence, so it is coded major revision; this call is borderline. R3 only co-signs another referee's report and does not say whose. R3 is assigned major revision because two of the three possible reports (R1, R2) were coded major revision; R3's true co-signed report cannot be identified from the file. R4 says the work suits a specialized journal, so it is coded reject; the word 'reject' is not used.
recommendations.label: contested
